Re-execute a `.replay` failure artifact.

A failing `largo run --interpret` writes a self-contained bundle under `target/replays/` — embedded source, scheduler seed and decision trace, input transcript, and the failure coordinate. Replaying it re-executes the program deterministically and reports whether the recorded failure still reproduces byte-identically, no longer fires (fixed), or diverged (the program or bundle changed since recording).

Bundles are portable and committable: a bundle checked into a project's test corpus is a permanent reproduction of the bug it recorded.

Usage: largo replay [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          Path to the `.replay` bundle

Options:
      --verify
          Treat divergence as a hard error (exit non-zero). Reproduced and fixed are both coherent verdicts; divergence never is

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo replay target/replays/main-1720000000.replay
  largo replay bug.replay --verify
